title: Price a tonne of CO2 in riders

blocks.text: A city transit agency can upgrade some of its bus depots this year. Each upgrade costs money and brings two benefits: more daily riders (better service from the depot) and less CO2 a year (electric buses charged there). The data team stores CO2 in kilograms a year, as the meters report it. After a long meeting the agency's board settled its trade-off in one sentence: "cutting one tonne of CO2 a year is worth as much to us as `riders_per_tonne` extra daily riders."

Write `weighted_choice(upgrades, budget, riders_per_tonne)` in `depots.py`: the set of upgrade names to fund, at most once each, with total cost within `budget`, that is best by the board's own trade-off. The model's variables and the budget row are written; the objective is yours.

Write the objective first, in notation: with $`U`$ the upgrades, $`x_u \in \{0, 1\}`$ whether upgrade $`u`$ is funded, $`r_u`$ its riders, $`g_u`$ its CO2 cut in kg and $`\pi`$ the board's price, what are the two weights, and in which units is each term? Then code it.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from depots import Upgrade, weighted_choice

stations = [Upgrade("Quay", 5, 350, 3000), Upgrade("Mill", 4, 120, 12000),
            Upgrade("Park", 3, 200, 1500), Upgrade("Dock", 2, 80, 6000)]

for price in (0, 15, 40):
    print(f"budget 8, {price} riders a tonne:", sorted(weighted_choice(stations, 8, price)))
print("budget 14, 15 riders a tonne:", sorted(weighted_choice(stations, 14, 15)))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Upgrade:
    name: str
    cost: int          # $k
    riders: int        # daily riders gained
    co2_kg: int        # kg of CO2 cut per year


def weighted_choice(upgrades: list[Upgrade], budget: int, riders_per_tonne: float) -> set[str]:
    """The upgrades to fund: the most riders plus CO2 cut, priced at `riders_per_tonne`, within budget."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="depots")
    x = {u.name: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{u.name}") for u in upgrades}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(u.cost * x[u.name] for u in upgrades) <= budget, name="budget")
    # TODO: the objective, both measures in one sum.
    model.maximize(mathopt.LinearExpression())
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    return {name for name, var in x.items() if result.variable_values(var) > 0.5}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    depots = [Upgrade("D1", 4, 300, 2000), Upgrade("D2", 3, 100, 9000), Upgrade("D3", 3, 250, 1000)]
    print(sorted(weighted_choice(depots, 6, 50)))

cases.says: when one choice is best for riders and for CO2 alike, it is chosen at any price
the CO2 data in kilograms is converted to the tonnes the price is quoted in
the price turns tonnes into riders, so it multiplies the CO2 term

origin.section: The Ratio Is a Price, So It Depends on the Units

concepts: a weighted sum of two linear objectives is one linear objective on the same model
the weight ratio is an exchange rate whose meaning depends on each objective's unit
